title: The Soft chair by the fire
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：soft　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 soft 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1980 the guide wrote of ① a soft chair by the fire in the guidebook, and everybody in the valley said at once that it was ② softer than the one named there the year before. Three days on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the guide, who never explained anything, had done it in the rain and gone home; it was the soft ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the softest chair by the fire anybody in the valley had ever seen, or so the guidebook for July 1974 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too soft to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the traveller who had come to help; the soft ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the map at the far ledge, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a soft voice of the nurse, and said that no traveller in his right mind would call it ⑥ as soft as the voice of the nurse they had once had in the old valley. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was soft or not, and he said so.

By 1987 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the guidebook. What the line asked for was ⑦ something soft, and nothing besides. The traveller from the next valley called the whole plan ⑧ quite soft; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the guidebook kept the names of the soft ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1990, without complaint, she wrote of another soft chair by the fire in the same guidebook, and the work, which took two days, seemed ⑨ softer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The softest voice of the nurse in the whole valley, she said in 1992, was the one she could never quite name; the soft ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 柔软（前置定语 a soft chair by the fire：1980 年向导在旅行手册里记下的那件柔软的椅子）
B. adj. 柔软／轻柔（比较级 softer than：文中两处，一处比火炉边柔软的椅子，一处比预想）
C. adj. 柔软／轻柔（最高级 the softest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 柔软（表语 too soft to do：母亲觉得它太柔软，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 轻柔（前置定语 a soft voice of the nurse：叔叔把整件事称作一桩轻柔的声音）
F. adj. 轻柔（同级比较 as soft as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩护士轻柔的声音相比）
G. adj. 轻柔（后置定语 something soft：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 轻柔（受程度副词修饰 quite soft：那位旅人的评价）

items.q: a soft chair by the fire
the softest chair by the fire anybody
a soft voice of the nurse
The softest voice of the nurse in

answers.why: soft 意为“柔软”，1980 年向导在旅行手册里记下的是“一件柔软的椅子”，此处作前置定语 a soft chair by the fire。
soft 意为“柔软”，此处用比较级 softer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
soft 意为“柔软”，旅行手册上 七月 那行字说它是山谷里最柔软的一件，故用最高级 the softest chair by the fire。
soft 意为“柔软”，母亲认为这件东西“太柔软了，谁也用不上”，too soft to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
soft 意为“轻柔”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩轻柔的声音”，此处作前置定语 a soft voice of the nurse。
soft 意为“轻柔”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩护士轻柔的声音一样轻柔”，同级比较用 as soft as。
soft 意为“轻柔”，旅行手册上那半行字要的是“轻柔的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something soft。
soft 意为“轻柔”，邻山谷来的那位旅人认为这套计划“相当轻柔”，quite 修饰原级 soft。
soft 意为“轻柔”，1990 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要轻柔”，故用比较级 softer than。
soft 意为“轻柔”，母亲 1992 年说的是“整个山谷里最轻柔的那一桩”，故用最高级 the softest voice of the nurse。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1980 年，向导在旅行手册里记下了一件柔软的椅子。（a soft chair by the fire）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更柔软。（softer than …）
母亲觉得它太柔软，谁也用不上。（too soft to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩轻柔的声音。（a soft voice of the nurse）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩护士轻柔的声音一样轻柔。（as soft as …）
到了 1987 年，旅行手册上只剩半行字：要的是一件轻柔的东西。（something soft）
answers: In 1980 the guide wrote of a soft chair by the fire in the guidebook.
Everybody said it was softer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too soft to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a soft voice of the nurse.
He said nobody would call it as soft as the voice of the nurse they had once had.
By 1987 the guidebook asked for nothing but something soft.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 soft 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1980 the guide wrote of a soft chair by the fire in the guidebook, and nobody forgot it.
It was the softest chair by the fire in the valley, or so the guidebook says.
My mother thought it too soft to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a soft voice of the nurse, and nobody argued with him.
The traveller from the next valley called the plan quite soft, and everybody laughed.
The soft ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
